historyItems.originalTitle: Nebius Lowers Outlook, Addresses Worries Over Financing AI Buildout
historyItems.originalSummary: By Kelly Cloonan Nebius Group lowered its full-year revenue outlook, citing a delay in some third-party capacity. The artificial-intelligence cloud company also addressed recent concerns over financing its buildout, emphasizing its momentum with customer prepayments. Nebius said Thursday it now expects full-year revenue to come in at the low end of its prior guidance range of $3 billion to $3.4 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet are forecasting $3.35 billion. The updated guidance factors in a portion of this year's revenue moving into next year, with some third-party capacity Nebius had expected to come online this year now scheduled for the first half of 2027, the company said. The contracts behind that capacity remain in place, the company said. Nebius also gave an initial outlook for next year, guiding for revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, compared with analyst projections of $12.09 billion. The company said the forecast reflects a conservative approach to the pace of its buildout, and that it continues to expect to bring online more than 1 gigawatt of new capacity each year. "Our focus remains on building a healthy, profitable business for the long term," Chief Executive Arkady Volozh said in a letter to shareholders. The guidance comes amid investor worries over how neocloud companies will finance their growing footprints. CoreWeave, whose borrowing costs have surged in recent weeks and helped spark the market jitters, eased some of those concerns earlier this week after reporting better-than-expected quarterly revenue. Volozh said Nebius is able to finance its buildout in a prudent way through customer prepayments and a healthy balance sheet, helped by a strategy that lets it command premium prices and terms, and bring down its costs of infrastructure from designing and building it itself. Nebius expects prepayments and financing against existing contracts with investment-grade customers to cover 75% to 85% of its capital expenditures in 2027, and has a wide range of other funding options available, Volozh said. "Our confidence in the fundamentals of what we are building has not changed, and the opportunity ahead of us is as large as it has ever been. We will keep going," Volozh said. Nebius shares slid 12% to $136.66 in premarket trading. Nebius reported a third-quarter loss of $37.5 million, or 13 cents a share, compared with a loss of $119.6 million, or 50 cents a share, a year earlier. Revenue surged by more than six-fold to $980.8 million, compared with analyst estimates of $907.2 million. Write to Kelly Cloonan at kelly.cloonan@wsj.com (END) Dow Jones Newswires 11-12-26 0838ET

historyItems.originalTitle: ULA suffers first outright failure with loss of Vulcan rocket carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
historyItems.originalSummary: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan, equipped with six solid rocket boosters, lifts off from Cape Canaveral's pad 41. A failure 10 minutes into flight resulted in the loss of 40 Amazon Leo satellites. Image: Michael Cain/Spaceflight Now In a major setback for United Launch Alliance, the company’s new heavy-lift Vulcan rocket carrying a batch of Amazon Leo internet satellites, malfunctioned during the climb to space Sunday, dooming the payload and throwing a costly wrench into the launch schedule of both companies. “Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 (at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station) suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit,” ULA said in a statement some 50 minutes after liftoff. “We will work closely with our customer and other appropriate organizations to find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action and return to flight as quickly as possible.” It was the first outright failure of a United Launch Alliance rocket since the company, a partnership between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, was formed in 2006. It wasn’t immediately known what went wrong, but the Vulcan, the rocket replacing ULA’s fleet of Atlas 5 rockets, will face a potentially significant grounding while engineers review telemetry and implement fixes for whatever caused the mishap. It was only the fifth flight of a Vulcan rocket and the first in nine months as ULA and booster-supplier Northrop Grumman worked to resolve problems with nozzles used by strap-on solid-fuel boosters that marred two earlier flights. The solids appeared to work normally Sunday, helping boost the rocket out of the dense lower atmosphere before burning out and falling away. The two methane-burning BE-4 engines powering the Vulcan’s first stage then continued the climb toward orbit, but they appeared to fire longer than expected based on ULA’s pre-launch timeline. After stage separation, the Vulcan’s hydrogen-fueled Centaur upper stage engines took over for a planned 12-minute 15-second burn. According to ULA’s update, something went wrong during that Centaur firing, but no additional details were immediately provided. Sunday’s launch was the first of 38 Vulcan flights purchased by Amazon to launch its Leo satellites, designed to compete head-to-head with Elon Musk’s Starlinks and other space-based internet providers. ULA already has launched eight LEO flights using Atlas 5 rockets.

historyItems.originalTitle: Aehr Test Systems, Inc. (AEHR) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
historyItems.originalSummary: Sifting through countless of stocks in the Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment industry can be tedious, and sometimes two stocks are just too similar to judge which is the better investment. If you’re on the fence about investing in Amkor Technology, Inc., Aehr Test Systems or Inc. because you’re not sure how they measure up, it’s important to compare them on a few factors before making your decision. Read on to learn how Amkor Technology, Inc., Aehr Test Systems and Inc. compare based on key financial metrics to determine which better meets your investment needs. About Amkor Technology, Inc., Aehr Test Systems and Inc. Amkor Technology, Inc. provides outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services in the United States, Japan, Europe, and the Asia Pacific. It offers turnkey packaging and test services, including semiconductor wafer bump, wafer probe, wafer back-grind, package design, packaging, burn-in, system-level and final test, and drop shipment services; flip chip scale package products for smartphones, tablets, and other mobile consumer electronic devices; flip chip stacked chip scale packages that are used to stack memory digital baseband, and as applications processors in mobile devices; flip-chip ball grid array packages for various networking, storage, computing, automotive, and consumer applications; and memory products for system memory or platform data storage. historyItems.title: SpaceX 歷史性首次捕捉 Starship 火箭上級
historyItems.summary: SpaceX has achieved a major milestone in its Starship programme by successfully catching the rocket's upper stage using giant mechanical arms attached to its launch tower. The spacecraft returned to Earth after spending 22.5 hours in space, marking the first successful recovery of the Ship through this technique. Starship completes 22.5-hour flight The 124-metre-tall Starship rocket lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase launch facility in Boca Chica, Texas, at 16:47 local time on Friday.
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX has achieved a major milestone in its Starship programme by successfully catching the rocket's upper stage using giant mechanical arms attached to its launch tower. The spacecraft returned to Earth after spending 22.5 hours in space, marking the first successful recovery of the Ship through this technique. However, the mission was only partially successful, as the rocket's lower section failed its planned recovery attempt. Starship completes 22.5-hour flight The 124-metre-tall Starship rocket lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase launch facility in Boca Chica, Texas, at 16:47 local time on Friday. This was the 15th test flight of the spacecraft and the first attempt to recover both sections of the rocket during the same mission. After reaching space, the upper stage, known as the Ship, deployed 26 satellites for SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation. It subsequently completed 14 orbits around Earth before beginning its return journey. The moment a Starship booster exploded during an attempted landing at SpaceX’s facility today. https://t.co/HoRscWHVH0 — распад и неуважение (@VictorKvert2008) November 14, 2026 &nbsp; How did SpaceX catch Starship? As the Ship approached its launch site, it hovered near the launch tower, where two enormous mechanical arms, nicknamed 'chopsticks', moved into position and secured the returning spacecraft. The arms are part of SpaceX's Mechazilla recovery system, which is designed to catch returning rocket stages instead of allowing them to land on the ground using conventional landing legs. This was the first time SpaceX successfully caught Starship's upper stage. The company had previously demonstrated the technique with its Super Heavy booster, which it had caught on three earlier test flights. What happened to Starship's booster? While the upper-stage recovery succeeded, the mission encountered a problem during the attempted recovery of the Super Heavy booster. The lower section was expected to return to the launch tower approximately six and a half minutes after liftoff. However, an automated abort system cancelled the catch attempt and diverted the booster towards the ocean. The booster hovered above the water before bursting into flames. Elon Musk later said on X that it was "slightly low on fuel". Why does SpaceX want to recover both stages? SpaceX aims to make Starship completely reusable to reduce the cost of launching payloads into space. Recovering both sections would allow the company to inspect, refuel and prepare the rocket for subsequent flights. The approach builds on the company's Falcon 9 programme, whose reusable boosters have helped reduce launch costs. Why is this important for NASA's Moon mission? Starship's development is closely linked to NASA's Artemis programme. SpaceX has a contract to develop a lunar lander based on Starship that could transport astronauts to the Moon's surface. However, the company must demonstrate reliable recovery and repeated operations before Starship can fulfil its ambitious role in future lunar missions.

historyItems.originalSummary: Baron Capital , an investment management company, released its third-quarter 2026 investor letter for its "Baron Global Opportunity Fund". The letter can be downloaded here . The fund gained 3.3% (Institutional Shares) in the quarter, outperforming the 1.6% gain for the MSCI ACWI Index (the Index) and the 0.5% decline for the MSCI ACWI Growth Index, the Fund's benchmarks. YTD, the Fund is up 24.6% vs. 13.0% and 10.1% gains for the benchmarks, respectively. Strong stock selection and sector allocation drove 172 bps of outperformance in the quarter. Information Technology and Health Care led sector returns, while Developed Markets led regional gains. The Fund remains optimistic about the potential of AI and the Space Economy despite geopolitical uncertainties and rising interest rates. Guided by its long-term strategy, the Fund remains optimistic about its portfolio's prospects and is patiently seeking new opportunities that trade at attractive discounts to intrinsic value. Additionally, reviewing the Fund's top five holdings could help identify its best picks for 2026.

NEW YORK , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SueWallSt alerts investors in Fluence Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ: FLNC ) of a pending securities class action on behalf of purchasers of Fluence Energy securities between November 24, 2025 and September 16, 2026. Find out if you may qualify to recover losses or contact Joseph E. Levi, Esq. at [email protected] or (888) SueWallSt. FLNC closed at $28.99 on February 4, 2026, and faltered to just $18.95 the following day, a decline of $10.04 per share, or about 34.63%. The complaint highlights two further declines of about $1.02, or 7.17% on August 6, 2026 and of $1.39, or about 15.36% on September 17, 2026. To be considered for lead plaintiff, investors must file by November 27, 2026. The Market Impact of Each FLNC Disclosure Day As averred, the decline unfolded in stages because Fluence Energy reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 outlook alongside the February 4, 2026 results and again on May 6, 2026. The pleading asserts that the Company did not disclose that delivering backlog and recognizing guided revenue depended on new contract manufacturing facilities that were not completed, not operational, or not capable of the assumed volumes. It further asserts that corrective measures at the Company's contract manufacturers were not remediating the production problems. The complaint charges that the August 5, 2026 report, which blamed weaker revenue on "production delays at new contract manufacturing facilities," and the September 16, 2026 update, which cited "continuing supply chain issues affecting the Company's U.S. production," each partially corrected those alleged misstatements. "Fluence Energy shareholders absorbed three heavy-volume selloffs in under eight months, and the complaint alleges each one followed news about contract manufacturing problems that had not been disclosed when guidance was set. About Amkor Technology, Inc., Aehr Test Systems and Inc. Amkor Technology, Inc. provides outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services in the United States, Japan, Europe, and the Asia Pacific. It offers turnkey packaging and test services, including semiconductor wafer bump, wafer probe, wafer back-grind, package design, packaging, burn-in, system-level and final test, and drop shipment services; flip chip scale package products for smartphones, tablets, and other mobile consumer electronic devices; flip chip stacked chip scale packages that are used to stack memory digital baseband, and as applications processors in mobile devices; flip-chip ball grid array packages for various networking, storage, computing, automotive, and consumer applications; and memory products for system memory or platform data storage. The company provides wafer-level CSP packages for power management, transceivers, sensors, wireless charging, codecs, and specialty silicon; wafer-level fan-out packages used in power management, transceivers, radar, and specialty silicon; silicon wafer integrated fan-out technology that replaces a laminate substrate with a thinner structure; leadframe packages for electronic devices and mixed-signal applications; and substrate-based wirebond packages used to connect a die to a substrate. Further, the company provides wafer, package, and system level test services, as well as burn-in test and test development services. It serves integrated device manufacturers, fabless semiconductor companies, original equipment manufacturers, and contract foundries. Amkor Technology, Inc. was founded in 1968 and is headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne Benefits From Strong Test Demand: Can It Beat KLAC & COHU?
historyItems.originalSummary: Teradyne TER is benefiting from strong semiconductor test demand, accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, and increasing complexity in advanced chip architectures. Rising demand for AI accelerators, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and high-performance computing solutions is strengthening the company's growth prospects and competitive position against KLA KLAC and Cohu COHU. Teradyne reported impressive third-quarter 2026 results, with revenues surging 70% year over year to $1.31 billion. Semiconductor Test revenues increased 77% to more than $1 billion, supported by robust demand for AI accelerators, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and power management solutions. Compute revenues grew nearly 50%, while memory revenues reached a record $301 million, reflecting strong demand for HBM and DRAM testing. Teradyne's expanding product portfolio is another key growth driver. The company's UltraFLEXplus platform is gaining traction as hyperscalers increasingly adopt dual-vendor testing strategies. Its recently introduced UltraVS64-HP, UltraPort-PCIe6 and Magnum E2 solutions strengthen its ability to address next-generation AI accelerators, high-speed connectivity and advanced memory testing requirements. Teradyne expects additional hyperscaler capacity purchases and compute-related revenue opportunities in 2027. Teradyne's expanding AI-driven opportunities and product innovations position it favorably to sustain momentum against KLAC and COHU. For the fourth quarter of 2026, Teradyne expects revenues between $1.25 billion and $1.35 billion. The midpoint of the guidance range stands at $1.30 billion.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX’s Starship Launch Today Could Lift the Stock
historyItems.originalSummary: If you find yourself in Texas during the next flight of SpaceX's massive Starship rocket , you may be in for quite a show. Anytime the world's largest rocket is due to get off the ground at SpaceX's Starbase headquarters in Boca Chica, a crowd is sure to form at the nearby South Padre Island . This time, though, it may not be just the launch of Starship that attracts spectators, but the possible return a day later of the rocket's upper section to South Texas. Up until now, SpaceX has sought to land the upper stage vehicle in distant oceans after it hits its objectives and completes its test flights. In some infamous cases, the vehicle has even accidentally exploded in the air mid-flight. For the first time, though, the plan is for both Starship's stages to travel back to Starbase after doing their jobs. And in the case of the upper stage, that dramatic landmark homecoming should take it over a large swath of Texas . Here's where you can watch SpaceX conduct its next Starship flight test from Starbase, Texas, as well as what to expect for a mission referred to as flight 15 . SpaceX, which tech mogul Elon Musk founded in 2002, is developing Starship to be a fully reusable transportation system, meaning both the rocket and vehicle can return to the ground for additional missions. Reaching 407 feet tall when fully stacked, Starship is regarded as the largest and most powerful launch vehicle ever developed. The rocket is composed of both the 236-foot lower stage booster known as Super Heavy that provides the initial burst of thrust at liftoff, and a 171-foot upper stage that flies in orbit. The third and latest prototype of Starship, known as Version 3 (V3) is still undergoing test flights as SpaceX races to have it ready for NASA's Artemis lunar landings and Musk's own dreams of crewed trips to Mars . Starship is also central to SpaceX's plans of expanding its Starlink satellite internet business. SpaceX is working toward a Friday, Nov. 13, launch of its Starship rocket, the company announced . The launch window is due to open from 4:45 to 6 p.m. CT. This time, though, spectators in Texas may want to make a point to not just catch the launch, but the return of the section of the rocket that flies in space nearly a day later (see more on that below).

historyItems.originalTitle: Nokia Federal Solutions awarded Department of War RAPID contract to advance multi-domain threat awareness
historyItems.originalSummary: CHANTILLY, Va., 13 November 2026 | 14:00 PM Europe/Amsterdam Nokia Federal Solutions awarded Department of War RAPID contract to advance multi-domain threat awareness Press Release Nokia Federal Solutions today announced that it has been awarded a contract under the Department of War's (DoW) RAPID project, managed by the FutureG Office within the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (OUSW(R&E)). The award supports Real-World Application Prototyping for ISAC Demonstration (RAPID), leveraging 5G and 6G infrastructure for object detection and tracking. Under the contract, Nokia Federal will develop, build and test integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) capabilities and demonstrate an end-to-end solution for the DoW's RAPID project. The effort supports the FutureG Office's mission by demonstrating how 5G and future 6G networks can be leveraged to improve threat detection and situational awareness, helping protect critical infrastructure against emerging threats. Built on Nokia's AI-RAN platform, the project will integrate Nokia and third-party applications for sensing and spectrum threat awareness. It will combine multiple sensing modalities and sensor fusion to help provide a more comprehensive picture of potential unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) threats. Subcontractors supporting the effort include Nokia affiliates, Texas Tech University, DeepSig, Hidden Level and Future Technologies. " The unmanned system threat is real. historyItems.summary: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan, equipped with six solid rocket boosters, stands ready for launch at Cape Canaveral's pad 41. The rocket will carry 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. Image: Michael Cain/Spaceflight Now. Update: Launch has now slipped to Sunday at 12:11 p.m.
historyItems.originalTitle: ULA delays to Sunday Vulcan rocket launch of 40 Leo satellites for Amazon
historyItems.originalSummary: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan, equipped with six solid rocket boosters, stands ready for launch at Cape Canaveral's pad 41. The rocket will carry 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. Image: Michael Cain/Spaceflight Now. Update: Launch has now slipped to Sunday at 12:11 p.m. EST (1711 UTC) due to a network communication issue between the ground and the rocket that could not be resolved in time for Saturday’s launch window. United Launch Alliance will try again Saturday to launch its Vulcan rocket after a power interruption at a nitrogen plant scrubbed Friday’s attempt, further postponing the 215-foot-tall vehicle’s return to flight after solid rocket booster nozzles failed on two of its first four missions. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station is now scheduled for 12:32:30 p.m. EST (1732:30 UTC) Saturday, Nov. 14. ULA said the rocket and the 40 Amazon Leo satellites it carries remain healthy. “The launch of a United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket carrying the Amazon [LV-01] mission is delayed due to a power interruption in the Air Liquide gaseous nitrogen plant which resulted in the loss of their high-pressure pumps,” ULA said in a statement Friday morning. “Without confirmation of sustained commodity flow, the team has decided to realign the launch to the back-up opportunity.” Spaceflight Now will have live coverage Saturday beginning 30 minutes prior to liftoff. ULA announced the delay at 8:41 a.m. EST, a little more than four hours before the originally scheduled Friday liftoff and after the launch team had begun loading liquid oxygen into the rocket’s Centaur 5 upper stage, according to the company’s live mission updates. Gaseous nitrogen is used to purge and pressurize systems on the rocket and launchpad. The one-day delay extends a nine-month wait since the most recent solid rocket booster malfunction prompted the U.S. government to pause its use of the non-reusable rocket for national security missions. The now-delayed mission serves a private customer, Amazon, which has tasked ULA with ferrying 40 broadband internet satellites to expand its Leo constellation. It’s the first of 38 Vulcan launches Amazon has purchased. ULA has not said how long Saturday’s launch window will last. The rocket will fly on a northeasterly trajectory upon leaving the pad.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
historyItems.originalSummary: Later today, SpaceX is planning the most ambitious test yet of its massive new rocket Starship. If all goes well, it will lift off from a pad in South Texas, circle the Earth and then land vertically at the same pad 22 and a half hours later. The test would be a major milestone for a rocket that company founder Elon Musk says he hopes will one day carry astronauts to Mars. But experts say the rapid development of Starship could also end up stranding one of the company's biggest boosters over the years: NASA. That's because as SpaceX ramps up its new rocket, it has said it will stop flying a much smaller one called Falcon 9. Falcon 9 launches the company's Dragon capsule, which is currently the only American spacecraft capable of ferrying NASA astronauts to and from the International Space Station. "Because Dragon has become such a successful and reliable vehicle, it became the de facto way for astronauts to get to orbit," said Caleb Henry, director of research at Quilty Space, a firm that tracks the space industry. According to a NASA announcement in September, the space agency has contracted with SpaceX for three additional flights to the International Space Station. That would only allow Dragon to fly through 2028, assuming the missions were flown consecutively in six month increments and no further flights are contracted with SpaceX.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX plans over $74 billion investment in Texas, Arizona AI campuses
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX (SPCX) pegs its Texas and Arizona AI campuses at over $74 billion, yet the shares barely moved because most of it is planned spending. Arizona is the riskier, larger half: a roughly $50 billion campus filed through shell company Tombstone Resources, with no contract backing promised jobs or bill cuts. A December 9 Cochise County zoning hearing decides whether the $74 billion plan holds or the Arizona half falls into doubt. On November 12, 2026, SpaceX ( NASDAQ:SPCX ) put a single price on its AI expansion. In a company update, it said a supercompute facility at Starbase in Texas' Rio Grande Valley and a campus in Cochise County, Arizona, together represent more than $74 billion in planned American investment.

historyItems.originalTitle: Building a rocket is hard. AST SpaceMobile thinks it’s “simple.”
historyItems.originalSummary: During an hour-long event on Thursday, Abel Avellan, the founder and chief executive of the telecommunications company AST SpaceMobile, laid out his vision for developing a large rocket to launch his Bluebird satellites into orbit. Avellan emphasized, over and over again, that AST plans to build a “simple” rocket. He paraphrased SpaceX founder Elon Musk several times, saying, “the best part is no part.” Avellan emphasized that AST has already procured engines for its proposed Blacklift rocket, asserting that engine development accounts for 80 percent of a typical rocket’s development cycle. “Of course rocket engineers are going to get mad with me, but you can simplify it as a big tank feeding engines,” he said of the rocket. “So big tanks—we know how to do them. We know how to do them. We know how to do them in composite.” I am not a rocket engineer, and I am not mad at Avellan. But he sure seems to be substantially underestimating the challenge of building rockets. Avellan also has a problem. AST SpaceMobile appears to be successful in building very large satellites, Bluebirds, that are capable of providing direct-to-cell capability from an orbit about 550km above Earth. The problem is there is a commercial launch crunch, and the company is struggling to get its satellites on orbit today, and projects to do so into the future. “We’re not doing this thing because we like rockets,” he said during the presentation. “We’re not doing this thing because we want to be in the launch business. We want this because we have so much demand of our satellites, and as you have seen it, we cannot get enough launches.” The Blacklift rocket will be “simple,” he said, because it will be solely tailored to lift five Bluebird satellites into low-Earth orbit at a time. It will have 20 metric tons of lift capacity, a reusable first stage, and launch twice a month from a pad at Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia that formerly served the Antares rocket. It will have all composite tanks and three stages. And, Avellan said, it will be ready to launch in 2028. If that timeline sounds preposterous, that’s because it is. However, Avellan believes AST has a workaround: It is committed to spending $1.3 billion to acquire enough engines for the first three Blacklift launches from Firefly Aerospace, as well as a license to manufacture additional engines over time. He is basing this argument on the Miranda first stage engine, which he said is “ready to fly.” But that’s not quite true. However, Miranda has not yet completed its formal qualification campaign, much less flown on an orbital rocket. Firefly chief executive Jason Kim said this week that qualification testing remains underway. Moreover, little is known publicly about the readiness of the upper stage engine, Vira, that AST is also acquiring from Firefly for its rocket.

historyItems.originalTitle: Ondas bets big on Israel with $1b. investment over past year
historyItems.originalSummary: Ondas has invested $1 billion in Israel, Dr. Judith Hocherman-Frommer, CTO and chief engineer of Ondas Autonomous Systems, announced at the UVID DroneTech 2026 conference at Expo Tel Aviv. “Investment in Israel is becoming mission critical,” she said, adding that the US-based company has acquired 27 defense-tech companies over the past 18 months, the majority being Israeli companies. The others are from the United States or Europe."We do not only acquire companies; we invest in each one to maximize its capabilities and create opportunities for collaboration among them to solve operational challenges in real time,” she added.The acquisitions are part of Ondas' broader push to build a vertically integrated defense technology company spanning the development, manufacturing, and deployment of autonomous systems. Its portfolio includes autonomous drones, counter-UAS systems, robotic ground platforms, unmanned aircraft, and systems for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions.The company's motto, she said, is “Bots before boots,” with autonomous systems leading and clearing the way ahead of the warfighter.According to Hocherman-Frommer, threats are evolving at a pace not seen before, within months rather than years, and therefore require fast, practical responses as well as strong integration between Israel's operational innovation and global manufacturing and deployment infrastructures.The modern battlefield is creating “a democratization of low-cost threats at massive scale, asymmetric warfare, and a constant learning race that demands flexibility and rapid adaptation. At the same time, these realities are colliding with multi-year development cycles and legacy architectures on the ground."In response, the defense industry needs to change its operating model, as “the response to rapidly evolving threats can no longer rely on development programs that take years to complete, nor on expensive, standalone missiles designed to counter swarms of low-cost drones."Instead, "There must be a shift toward developing simpler and faster systems, manufacturing large quantities at high quality and affordable cost, and advancing toward autonomy, where systems operate independently while human operators provide high-level oversight."“Speed is the new strategic advantage,” she stressed.Digital BatHocherman-Frommer's comments came just days after Ondas announced that it had received a purchase order under its Digital Bat program, a next-generation tactical attack drone designed to meet what the company believes could become demand for tens of thousands of affordable autonomous strike systems. The company said the order marks a transition from development toward serial production and large-scale manufacturing. Ondas said it plans to leverage its pending acquisition of ARAN Defense, an Israeli engineering and manufacturing company, to establish dedicated production lines capable of manufacturing thousands of systems. historyItems.originalTitle: TSMC Approves Up to $1 Billion Investment Plan in Anthropic, OpenAI
historyItems.originalSummary: Android Headlines / Tech News / TSMC Backs Anthropic and OpenAI With $1 Billion Investment TSMC’s board has approved an investment plan of up to $1 billion in two AI companies, OpenAI and Anthropic. It plans to invest $500 million in Anthropic IPO and another $500 million in OpenAI’s preferred stock. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has approved an investment of $1 billion in two AI companies, OpenAI and Anthropic. The world’s largest contract chipmaker plans to invest $500 million in each company. It looks forward to expanding financial ties with two well-known names in the AI industry, especially as AI demand grows. In a recent development, TSMC’s board has approved a $500 million investment in Anthropic’s upcoming Initial Public Offering (IPO). Moreover, the top management has also cleared an investment of up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock. With this financial step, the company seeks a stake in both AI companies. Anthropic has priced its IPO at between $70 and $78 per share. The tech giant is targeting a total valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. On the other hand, the Claude developer is raising another $26 billion through a separate private placement. Multiple companies worldwide are backing the funding. The list includes Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia, AMD, and Microsoft. TSMC’s investment timing is particularly noticeable because it comes amid surging demand for AI chips. It already plays an important role in the AI industry and with the following step, it wants to further strengthen its position. The company is a key supplier to Nvidia, whose graphics processors are widely used to train and run AI models. TSMC has been breaking records in terms of overall growth and revenue. For reference, it recently reported its sixth consecutive quarter of record profit last month and said demand for AI-related chips remained “extremely robust”. What’s even more surprising is that it expects its revenue to grow further by 44% in 2026. The Taiwanese company recently said that the demand is so strong that its current manufacturing capacity is falling short of fulfilling it. To address this, TSMC is investing $265 billion in manufacturing facilities in Arizona . It is also exploring projects in Texas. In a nutshell, the company is going all out on AI, whether in the form of expanding its manufacturing capacity or investing $1 billion in AI companies.

As Treasury yields surged following the government data release, equities faced broad-based downward pressure, highlighting market sensitivity to persistent macroeconomic headwinds. The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. historyItems.originalSummary: Ge Vernova Inc (GEV) opened down by 7.06%. The Utilities sector is down by 1.54%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Ge Vernova Inc (GEV) down 7.06%; Nextera Energy Inc (NEE) down 0.71%; Eversource Energy (ES) down 0.75%. GE Vernova experienced pronounced downward pressure during the session, driven primarily by aggressive profit-taking and multiple compression across the power generation and electrical infrastructure sectors. After an extended period of outperformance fueled by the structural narrative surrounding artificial intelligence data center power demand and global grid modernization, elevated expectations have heightened sensitivity to any friction in project execution and capital expenditure cycles. A key catalyst behind the sell-off centers on renewed scrutiny over segment profitability, particularly surrounding the wind division. Persistent challenges in offshore wind project delivery, supply chain bottlenecks, and contract restructuring risks continue to act as an overhang on consolidated margins. While the company has made meaningful progress in de-risking its legacy offshore backlog, institutional investors remain cautious regarding the potential for further margin dilution or unexpected warranty charges before the segment achieves sustainable profitability. Simultaneously, broader industry dynamics within gas power and electrification equipment point to a pause in momentum. Despite robust order backlogs and favorable pricing power for heavy-duty gas turbines and grid solutions, market participants are increasingly focused on multi-year delivery timelines and the potential for utility customers to face regulatory or interconnection delays. Any indication of a moderated conversion pace from order book to revenue recognition leaves richly valued names susceptible to rapid valuation resets. Macroeconomic conditions and institutional positioning amplified the downward move. Upward pressure on benchmark yields and shifting expectations regarding federal energy policy and clean energy incentives prompted institutional desks to trim exposure to capital-intensive, high-valuation industrial names. Quantitative strategies and portfolio rebalancing away from momentum leadership into defensive value further accelerated intraday selling volume. Looking ahead, institutional focus will center on margin expansion trajectory within Electrification, cash flow conversion in the Power segment, and clear evidence of de-risking within Wind operations. While the long-term secular demand for power generation and transmission capacity remains intact, near-term price discovery will likely depend on management demonstrating sustained operating leverage and execution consistency across all business units. historyItems.originalTitle: Will it snow? Latest on potential nor’easter headed for Philly, NYC and DC
historyItems.originalSummary: An incoming storm is set to deliver the first snow of the season to parts of New England, though the Boston area will mainly contend with a cold, windswept rain starting Thursday. Several inches of wet snow are forecast for the highest elevations of Massachusetts and Northern New England. This system is set to eventually slide off the Mid-Atlantic coast late Thursday and develop into a nor’easter, bringing more rain, wind, and some wet snow through Friday. But unlike the other nor’easters we’ve seen this fall, we should avoid major impacts like coastal flooding. This one is more of an inconvenience for Greater Boston and Southern New England. • Snow — This storm holds a decent shot of delivering a coating to a couple of inches of snow along Route 2, west of I-495, and a coating to 3 inches of wet snow in a few higher-elevation spots across the Berkshires, northern Worcester County, and most of Vermont, New Hampshire, and Maine, with isolated spots seeing 3 to 6 inches across the highest terrain. • Rain — For the lower elevations and by the coast, it just won’t be that cold for widespread snow. Greater Boston should end up with about a half inch of cold, windswept rain, a lot less than what we experienced last week . The same rain scenario plays out as you head south to Cape Cod, the South Coast, and Rhode Island.

historyItems.originalTitle: Kratos and Seagate Space Partner to Advance Mobile Offshore Launch Capabilities for National Security Missions
historyItems.originalSummary: A photo accompanying this announcement is available at https://www.globenewswire.com/NewsRoom/AttachmentNg/6bce8d6c-8a04-4d2e-bad7-c7d636371732 SAN DIEGO, Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: KTOS), a technology company in defense, national security, and global markets, today announced a long-term agreement with Seagate Space for use of the company’s initial Gateway ™ offshore launch platform. The agreement supports Kratos’ planned first mission from the platform in 2027, with multiple additional launches anticipated in subsequent years. The partnership aligns Kratos’ mission of being first to market and proven record of delivering real, mission-relevant products and systems, including hypersonic test and other vehicles, rocket systems, propulsion technologies, target vehicles, and launch services, with Seagate Space’s modular, mobile offshore platform infrastructure. The Gateway series vessels are designed to provide flexible sea-based platforms to complement traditional land-based launch sites and test ranges. The announcement coincides with Seagate Space’s execution of its first Gateway platform construction contract, advancing into physical construction and toward future operational readiness.

historyItems.originalTitle: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy
historyItems.originalSummary: The artificial intelligence semiconductor giant Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into its CEO, Jensen Huang, after he acknowledged a romantic relationship with businesswoman Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le — who is suspected of spying for the Chinese government. The tech mogul is not only one of the most powerful business leaders in the United States and the artificial intelligence sector; he also maintains a close relationship with U.S. President Donald Trump, who said Sunday that Huang is an “honorable guy” and should remain in his position. The executive, who will continue to lead the company — at least for the time being — sent a message to the tech giant’s employees on Sunday after U.S. media outlets published new details about the romantic relationship. In it, he admitted to being unfaithful to his wife. “I owe my family and all of you an apology... There is no excuse for what I did,” he wrote. “To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.” The explosive situation began to come to light last month, when The New York Times broke the story about suspicions that Jensen Huang may have been the target of a Chinese espionage operation through his relationship with Huang Le. U.S. officials had concluded last year — as reported by the Times and later by other outlets — that Alice Huang, then a senior executive at Megaspeed International, had shared information with the Chinese government while collaborating with Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company, on the construction of data centers in Asia. U.S. investigators had launched their probe amid suspicions that Megaspeed helped Beijing gain access to advanced artificial intelligence semiconductors, the shipment of which to China is prohibited. The Singapore-based company had purchased enormous quantities of these chips from Nvidia: $4.8 billion worth over the past two years. Alice Huang was responsible for these purchasing operations at Megaspeed. Her biography indicates that she worked in China as a television journalist before becoming an executive at the Singapore-based company. According to the Times, last spring Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the drafting of a classified memorandum detailing intelligence that showed Alice Huang had been recruited by the Chinese Ministry of State Security to lure Jensen Huang into a trap. That document circulated shortly before Trump’s visit to China in May. The tech company’s board of directors stated in a press release that it has no reason to believe that the company’s secrets or U.S. national security have been compromised. “Today’s news will not slow Nvidia,” said a spokesperson for the tech giant. “Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.” In its statement, the board of directors specifies that an independent committee, which will be supported by “outside independent counsel,” will conduct the investigation. historyItems.originalTitle: When will it snow in New York? Latest forecast shows late-week storm potential
historyItems.originalSummary: New Yorkers could get a more noticeable taste of winter late this week as colder air spreads into the state and a developing storm potentially brings rain and snow. The latest forecasts do not support calling this a major statewide snowstorm. However, the National Weather Service is now monitoring a late-week system that could produce measurable snow in higher elevations of central and eastern New York. Lower elevations and coastal communities are more likely to receive rain, although the forecast remains uncertain. Before that system arrives, much of the state will experience seasonable to relatively mild weather. Scattered rain showers will affect parts of upstate New York through Monday, followed by a period of quieter weather in many areas. Some snow could reach parts of New York late this week, but it is too early to determine where it will accumulate or whether the storm will become disruptive. The National Weather Service in Binghamton said a clipper-type system could move into the Ohio Valley Wednesday and Thursday before potentially helping form a coastal storm by Friday. The forecast includes chances for rain and snow Thursday and Friday, with some rain and snow showers potentially lingering into Saturday. Higher elevations would have the best chance of seeing measurable snow if the storm tracks south of the region, allowing colder air to become established. The Catskills and higher terrain of central New York are among the areas to watch. Uncertainty remains high because forecast models differ on the storm's track. Even relatively small changes could determine whether a location receives snow, a rain-snow mix or primarily rain. The National Weather Service's winter weather forecasts provide snowfall projections extending out to 72 hours, including expected accumulation and lower- and higher-end possibilities. Western New York will remain unsettled into Monday, but the precipitation is initially expected to fall as rain.

historyItems.summary: AST SpaceMobile will build its own reusable Blacklift rocket with Firefly engines, sending Firefly shares up 37% while AST hit a 52-week low. Alphabet held about 9 million AST shares, worth roughly $289 million, as AST takes on rocket costs and dilution after a $231 million quarterly loss. Firefly's engine deal tops $1.3 billion, with AST paying about $800 million upfront in cash and shares that dilute current holders. Before the open on November 6, 2026, AST SpaceMobile ( NASDAQ:ASTS ) said it will build its own rocket, Blacklift, to launch its BlueBird satellites starting in late 2028.

historyItems.originalTitle: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose over $420 billion in combined market cap after midterms
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX and Tesla shares fell about 9% and 11%, respectively, on Thursday afternoon as investors worried that Elon Musk could face new congressional investigations and his companies could encounter stricter regulation after the US midterm elections.As if the election results were not enough, which saw the Republican Party, which Musk poured nearly half a billion into, being pummelled out of the US Congress, the turmoil at the bourse may just be the beginning of the world's richest man's chagrin.The declines, which coincided with a broader technology-sector sell-off, pushed combined market-cap losses for SpaceX and Tesla to more than $420 billion since Tuesday’s close.As per a CNBC report, by the close of trading on Thursday, SpaceX and Tesla had lost a combined approximately $456 billion in market capitalisation.According to Forbes, which keeps a reliable database of the richest in the world, Musk’s net worth, which exceeded $1 trillion after SpaceX’s initial public offering in June, has now fallen below $800 billion. He lost about $90 billion over the past week but remains the world’s richest person.Musk was the largest donor to Republican candidates and causes during the midterms, contributing more than $470 million, the Financial Times first reported.Despite his support for the GOP’s fundraising efforts, most of the candidates Musk backed lost their races.Democrats secured control of both the House and Senate. In Texas, home to both Tesla and SpaceX, Democratic Sen.-elect James Talarico and Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa defeated longtime Musk allies: state Attorney General Ken Paxton and Gov. Greg Abbott.Tesla and SpaceX are expanding their AI infrastructure in Texas and plan to build Terafab, a massive complex in Grimes County that will house both a data center and a sprawling semiconductor factory.According to company job postings, SpaceX also intends to develop a “supercomputer” at Starbase, its launch facility and company town in Texas.Deutsche Bank analysts, who spoke to CNBC, have warned that SpaceX’s computing expansion in Texas may face delays. They said the company could need to raise capital spending to comply with stricter regulations expected to govern data centre development.CNN first reported, citing an aide to a Democratic senator, that Musk and SpaceX had been instructed to retain records related to restrictions on a military version of Starlink in Ukraine. Those restrictions limited Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian attacks.Regulatory scrutiny could also jeopardise Musk’s proposed merger of SpaceX and Tesla, an idea he has promoted while acknowledging that it would first require shareholder approval.Read Also: Hyundai cars can now cut your insurance premium by up to 15% if you drive safely

He lost about $90 billion over the past week but remains the world’s richest person.Musk was the largest donor to Republican candidates and causes during the midterms, contributing more than $470 million, the Financial Times first reported.Despite his support for the GOP’s fundraising efforts, most of the candidates Musk backed lost their races.Democrats secured control of both the House and Senate. In Texas, home to both Tesla and SpaceX, Democratic Sen.-elect James Talarico and Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa defeated longtime Musk allies: state Attorney General Ken Paxton and Gov. Greg Abbott.Tesla and SpaceX are expanding their AI infrastructure in Texas and plan to build Terafab, a massive complex in Grimes County that will house both a data center and a sprawling semiconductor factory.According to company job postings, SpaceX also intends to develop a “supercomputer” at Starbase, its launch facility and company town in Texas.Deutsche Bank analysts, who spoke to CNBC, have warned that SpaceX’s computing expansion in Texas may face delays. They said the company could need to raise capital spending to comply with stricter regulations expected to govern data centre development.CNN first reported, citing an aide to a Democratic senator, that Musk and SpaceX had been instructed to retain records related to restrictions on a military version of Starlink in Ukraine. Those restrictions limited Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian attacks.Regulatory scrutiny could also jeopardise Musk’s proposed merger of SpaceX and Tesla, an idea he has promoted while acknowledging that it would first require shareholder approval.Read Also: Hyundai cars can now cut your insurance premium by up to 15% if you drive safely

historyItems.originalTitle: US proposes space launch rule changes in potential boost for SpaceX
historyItems.originalSummary: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposed changes to commercial space launch and re-entry rules. The move aims to reduce licensing delays and support a rapid rise in launch activity across the country.The proposals could particularly benefit Elon Musk’s SpaceX and Jeff Bezos’s Blue Origin. Both companies operate high-frequency launch programs and require repeated regulatory approvals for rockets, satellites and reusable vehicles..What the FAA Proposes.The FAA has put forward three key changes. First, operators would gain flexibility to switch off a rocket’s flight-termination system earlier in a mission and reactivate it later, provided they meet the agency’s safety conditions for that phase.Second, the regulator proposes clearer rules on when a launch must be aborted. The revised language would explain how companies should assess the risks of ending a flight early versus allowing it to continue after it can no longer achieve its objective.Third, the FAA wants to simplify how operators assess spacecraft breakup during uncontrolled re-entry. Companies could use existing debris analyses to show that fragments are unlikely to cause multiple casualties on the ground..A Boost for SpaceX.The changes would make launch approvals easier for SpaceX and Blue Origin, according to the FAA. SpaceX, which dominates US commercial launch activity, stands to gain the most since it conducts missions at a far higher cadence than its rivals.Faster approvals could help SpaceX expand Starlink satellite deployments, accelerate Starship development and reduce waiting periods between missions. Blue Origin could also benefit as it scales its New Glenn rocket program.The proposals follow earlier FAA moves to allow electronic launch applications, combine three safety analyses into one submission and give operators greater flexibility in demonstrating safe operations..Preparing for Higher Launch Volumes.The White House wants at least 1,000 commercial launches and re-entries annually by 2030. That target compares with 178 launches last year and marks a tenfold increase from 2013.To manage this growth, the FAA is expanding its Office of Commercial Space Transportation. It has named an associate administrator and is hiring aerospace engineers to speed up safety reviews and mission authorisations.The agency also plans a broader overhaul of its space-licensing framework beginning in 2027. The initiative signals a shift towards a more predictable and scalable regulatory system for the commercial space economy.Also Read: Qualcomm to Supply 5G Technology for SpaceX's Nationwide Network.Join our WhatsApp Channel to get the latest news, exclusives and videos on WhatsApp

historyItems.originalTitle: Micron Pauses Work on $4.5 Billion Taiwan Plant After Labor Spat
historyItems.originalSummary: Micron Technology Inc has suspended plans for a memory chip plant in Taiwan due to a protracted labor dispute, according to people familiar with the matter, throwing into question the fate of a major production base for crucial artificial intelligence (AI) components. The US company has all but halted construction of a plant in Taoyuan, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the deliberations are private. Executives are concerned about mounting uncertainties, including the risk that an agreement with a local labor union will get overturned. Micron has informed Taiwanese officials and a supplier about its plans to suspend construction in the city, the people said. Tensions between Micron and its workers flared this year after employees demanded higher compensation, seeking more of the record profits generated from the AI build-out. The potential disruption to Micron’s plans in Taiwan — an island that produces three-fifths of the US firm’s conventional chips — threatens to further cloud a market already grappling with endemic shortages of memory. Micron — which has invested close to US$50 billion in Taiwan over three decades — had planned on making high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and DRAM at the new Taoyuan plant using top-end equipment from ASML Holding NV. While it isn’t considered a giant facility by modern standards, those components are intertwined with Nvidia Corp accelerators and the global AI data center boom, and in such short supply that prices are skyrocketing. “Taiwan plays an important role in Micron’s global footprint, and our operations today continue as normal,” Micron said in a statement, without addressing questions about the Taoyuan complex. “We are confident in maintaining business continuity for our customers.” Micron secured a deal with the bigger of its two unions last month, but the company may need to renegotiate because some employees are balking at the terms, according to the people. The suspension raises the possibility Micron will reconsider plans for its broader manufacturing hub in Taiwan, which helps it compete with South Korea’s Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix Inc, and China’s CXMT Corp (長鑫存儲). Micron had budgeted US$3 billion to US$4.5 billion toward the Taoyuan complex, which included purchases of ASML gear, one of the people said. There’s still some minor work being done on the site to ensure its safety, but construction will freeze after that, the people added. Dubbed Fab 11E, it was previously scheduled to come online in 2028. Micron is Taiwan’s largest foreign investor, and it would be a major blow to the island if the company scaled back there. Taiwan’s economy and stock market have gotten a boost from the AI boom, with the likes of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. building plants at an unprecedented pace. Yet its viability as a long-term investment destination is at risk from potential Chinese military intervention.

historyItems.originalSummary: Viavi Solutions Inc ( (VIAV) ) has held its Q1 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call. Viavi Solutions delivered a strongly positive fiscal first-quarter performance, beating revenue, margin and earnings guidance while benefiting from powerful data-center and aerospace demand. Weak wireless spending, seasonally softer OSP revenue ahead and lower cash balances were the main concerns, but management raised its near-term growth outlook. Viavi reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $469.3 million, above its $450 million to $460 million target. Revenue rose 5.9% sequentially and 56.9% from a year earlier, reflecting broad strength across key markets. Operating margin reached 29%, ahead of the 26.7% to 27.5% forecast and up sharply from both prior periods. Earnings per share came in at $0.47, exceeding guidance of $0.40 to $0.42 and increasing $0.32 year over year. A tariff refund provided an approximately 110-basis-point boost to operating margin and added about $0.02 to EPS. Those benefits were partly offset by an additional week of certain variable expenses, making the quarter’s underlying performance important to investors. NSC revenue climbed 74.1% year over year to $376.1 million, beating guidance of $360 million to $368 million. Demand for lab, production and field products was supported by data-center expansion, the Spirent product lines and strong aerospace and defense activity. NSC gross margin rose 310 basis points year over year to 66.2%, helped by the tariff refund and a favorable product mix. Operating margin expanded to 25.5% from 8.2%, exceeding guidance as higher revenue produced stronger operating leverage. OSP revenue increased 12.2% year over year to $93 million, above its $90 million to $92 million target. Growth came from 3D sensing, anti-counterfeiting and other products, while operating margin reached 43.2%, up six percentage points from a year earlier. Operating cash flow more than tripled to $104.7 million from $31 million in the comparable period. Management attributed the improvement to higher net income and the timing of working-capital movements. Viavi repurchased about 3.95 million shares for approximately $150 million, at an average price of $37.98. With roughly $18 million remaining under the existing authorization, the board approved a new $500 million plan, while keeping organic investment and potential acquisitions as capital-allocation priorities.
